chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Rafaa'ah bin Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man to whom severe illness strikes before he enters Makkah. He said: 'He should not enter it except in Ihram.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَامٍ: Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who becomes severely ill before reaching the Miqat?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through the chain of Sahl ibn Ziyad, this hadith clarifies that severe illness does not exempt a pilgrim from the obligation of entering Makkah in a state of Ihram if they have not yet crossed their designated Miqat. This ruling underscores the principle that the state of consecration is tied to the geographic boundary rather than the physical condition of the traveler, ensuring the validity of the Hajj or Umrah ritual.
